concepts.why: Secular scholar / all readers: Isaiah 40:13 asks who has directed the Spirit of the LORD; the verse says nothing of creating or sending. It shares the word and is not the concept (the creation context is in v.12, not the verse). Gen 1:2 stays: the Berean reads 'Spirit of God'; the Hebrew ruach elohim can also be read 'wind', so the card should not lean on it alone, but beside Job 33:4 and Ps 104:30 it holds.

concepts.name: The Spirit among them, and nowhere to flee from
concepts.why: Name against passages (all readers): 'Where can I go to escape Your Spirit?' is Ps 139:7 only. Neh 9:20, Isa 63:11, 63:14 and Hag 2:5 say the Spirit was given, set and remains among the people; none speaks of escaping. A plain label that covers both halves (the Spirit with His people; no place to flee it) fits all five. If the owner wants the texts' own words, 'And My Spirit remains among you' (Hag 2:5) covers four of the five and Ps 139:7 should then move to its own line elsewhere.

note_fixes: Genesis 41:38: extend the passage to 41:38-39 so that 'discerning and wise' is in the verse the card shows; v.38 alone has the Spirit but not wisdom. Alternatively drop it.
concepts.why: Name against passages (secular scholar, Jewish reader of the Hebrew): Pharaoh's v.38 does not say wisdom; v.39 does. Eph 1:17 'a spirit of wisdom and revelation' is lower-case in the Greek tradition and readers (Reformed, Catholic, Orthodox) part on whether it names the Holy Spirit; the lower-case concept name already handles it, so keep it, but the note must not capitalise it (the quotation keeps the Berean's 'spirit', which is fine).

Secular / Jewish reader of the Hebrew: Gen 6:3 says the Spirit 'will not contend', a verb (yadon) whose sense is uncertain in the Hebrew and rendered differently across translations; it does not say the Spirit was taken or departed, which is what the name and the other two passages say. It rests on one translation's reading. Job 34:14-15 ('withdraw His Spirit and breath') says withdrawal and may be added here in its place. Placing Ps 51:11 beside 1 Sam 16:14 is right: the text is left to stand beside Eph 4:30 and Isa 59:21 without a verdict on perseverance.

note_fixes: Micah 3:8: the note quotes only 'to declare to Jacob his transgression and to Israel his sin', which has no Spirit in it; quote 'I am filled with power by the Spirit of the LORD, with justice and courage, to declare to Jacob his transgression' (an exact stretch of the verse) so the Spirit is in the note.
concepts.why: Isa 40:7 in the Berean says 'the breath of the LORD', not Spirit, and the verse says nothing of judgment by a Spirit; it shares a word at most. Pentecostal / Charismatic and Baptist: Matt 3:11-12 under a name about judgment and fire reads 'Holy Spirit and with fire' as judgment, while Acts 2:3-4 (the Fire secondary) and Luke 3:16 (concept 19) set fire beside tongues and baptism. This is acceptable as an overlap because the verse itself carries v.12, but the name must stay Isaiah's words and not be extended.

Secular scholar / Jewish reader of the Hebrew: in Isa 48:16 the Hebrew can be read 'the Lord GOD has sent me and His Spirit' (the Spirit as a second one sent), and the speaker is not identified. The Berean's 'accompanied by' is one translation's reading; the verse also does not say the Spirit rests on or is put on anyone, which the name and the other three passages do say. Drop it.

Name against passages and all nine readers: the name is 'The Spirit of the Lord is on Me'; Rom 1:4 ('Spirit of holiness'), Heb 9:14 ('the eternal Spirit') and 1 Tim 3:16 ('vindicated by the Spirit') do not say the Spirit is on Him, and the Berean's capital S is the translators' reading of a Greek word (pneuma, 'spirit of holiness', 'in spirit') that Reformed, Catholic, Orthodox and academic readers take differently (the Holy Spirit; or Christ's own spirit). The drafter dropped 1 Cor 15:45 on exactly this ground; the same standard removes these three. They go to the missing sub-theme named below, in lower case.

concepts.name: Baptized with the Holy Spirit
concepts.why: Pentecostal / Charismatic and Baptist: the name 'He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit' fixes the baptizer as 'He' and the tense as future, then places 1 Cor 12:13 ('in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body', past tense, agent disputed between 'by' and 'in' one Spirit) under it as if it were the same event as the Gospels' and Acts 1:5's promise. Whether it is the same event is exactly where the traditions part. Acts 1:5's own words 'baptized with the Holy Spirit' name the thing without deciding the agent or the tense, and let the six passages stand side by side as the drafter intends. The passages do not change.

note_fixes: Acts 2:39: the verse has 'this promise' but not the Spirit; extend to 2:38-39 (or drop it). Acts 2:38 names the gift and v.39 the promise, and without v.38 the card shows a promise with no content.
concepts.why: Name against passages: Acts 2:39 does not say what the promise is. Baptist (often dispensational) and Pentecostal readers part on how far 'to all who are far off' reaches; the text should show it with its referent in view and nothing more.

note_fixes: Acts 19:2: the note ends 'when you became believers', the Berean's rendering of a Greek aorist participle that other translations give 'since you believed' / 'after'. This verse is where Baptist and Pentecostal readers part on when the Spirit is received. Quote only the part both sides read alike: 'Did you receive the Holy Spirit'. Check against MACULA.
concepts.why: Baptist and Pentecostal: the rest of the set is balanced (Acts 8 after baptism, 10:44 before it, 19:6 with hands, 8:16 'had simply been baptized'; and Rom 8:9, Eph 1:13, Gal 3:2 sit elsewhere in the outline) and nothing in the name takes a side. Only the one translators' word at 19:2 leans, so the note is trimmed to what the verse says in both.

note_fixes: Acts 2:38: trim the note to 'you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit'. The full note also carries 'be baptized ... for the forgiveness of your sins', where 'for' renders a Greek preposition (eis) that Baptist, Lutheran, Catholic, Orthodox and Reformed readers take differently, and the concept is the gift, not that clause. The verse itself is still shown in full.
concepts.why: Baptist / free church versus Lutheran / Catholic / Orthodox: a note quoting only the part the concept needs avoids making the card an argument about baptism. The set of passages is balanced (Luke 11:13 'to those who ask', Acts 5:32 'those who obey', Gal 3:2 'hearing with faith').

concepts.name: The Spirit directing the way
concepts.why: Name against passages: 'Sent forth by the Holy Spirit' is Acts 13:4 only. Acts 16:6 (the Spirit prevented them), 21:4 (told Paul not to go), 15:28 (a decision of the council), 8:29 and 10:19 (a word to one man) are not sendings. A plain label covers them; keep 20:22-23 and 21:4 side by side as drafted, since they pull opposite ways in the text and that is honest. If the owner prefers the texts' own words, 'It seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us' (Acts 15:28) is the closest to the whole set.

note_fixes: 1 Corinthians 13:8: the note singles out 'where there are tongues, they will be restrained'; quote the whole verse so prophecies, tongues and knowledge stand together. The Berean's 'restrained' renders a Greek verb (pausontai) usually given 'cease'; this is the exact point where cessationist and continuationist readers part, so check MACULA and the verse as shown for the translators' word.

ADD Acts 2:6 (each one heard them speaking in his own language) and 1 Corinthians 14:18-19 and 14:22. As drafted the set has 14:2, 14:5 and 14:39 on one side and 12:30 and 13:8 on the other; the verses a Baptist (and a Reformed, Lutheran) reader would look for and a Pentecostal reader would look for are 14:19 ('five words with my mind') and 14:18, and Acts 2:6 is central to what the tongues at Pentecost were.
ADD 1 Corinthians 14:4 ('He who speaks in a tongue edifies himself') beside 14:5 if the owner wants the Pentecostal side as fully as 12:30 gives the other.
concepts.why: Pentecostal / Charismatic and Baptist / Reformed: the drafter's account says 12:30 and 13:8 stand beside 14:5 and 14:39. They do, but the passages under 'They spoke in tongues' lean slightly toward continuance without the verses that limit tongues or specify their meaning (14:19, 14:22, Acts 2:6).

note_fixes: 1 Corinthians 12:3: the ellipsis hides what is said ('Jesus is Lord'). Quote 'no one can say, “Jesus is Lord,” except by the Holy Spirit' (an exact stretch of the verse).
concepts.why: A note with an ellipsis that removes the thing tested is an incomplete quotation of its verse; the rest of the concept is sound.

Reformed, Catholic, Orthodox, academic scholar: the drafter dropped 1 Cor 15:45 because the Berean's reading and the original differ on what the word names; 1 Pet 3:18 ('made alive in the Spirit', Greek pneumati) is as disputed as that verse (Holy Spirit; Christ's own spirit; the sphere of resurrection) and the same ground applies. It goes to the lower-case sub-theme named below. Ezek 37:5-10 stays: the Berean says 'breath' where it should and 'My Spirit' only at 37:14.

Academic scholar, Reformed, Orthodox: in 2 Cor 12:18 'walk in the same Spirit' (Greek pneumati) is read by some as Paul's and Titus's shared disposition and by others as the Holy Spirit; the Berean's capital is the translators' reading, and the verse is about Titus's conduct, not walking by the Spirit as the name and the other three say. Drop it on the same ground as 1 Cor 15:45.

concepts.name: The fruit of the Spirit is love
concepts.why: Name against passages: 'fruit' is Gal 5:22-23 only. Rom 15:30, 2 Cor 6:6 and Col 1:8 say love by or in the Spirit; none says fruit. Gal 5:22's own first word, 'love', is what all four hold, and 'joy' has its own concept (40), so the name keeps the texts' words and fits every passage.

Name against passages: Rev 1:10 ('I was in the Spirit') is the seer's state at the time of a vision; it is neither worship nor prayer. It belongs with the vision passages (see missing: 'In the Spirit', with Rev 4:2 and 21:10).

secondary_or_links: Orthodox / Catholic: on the procession the outline is balanced as it stands. John 15:26 is quoted whole under 'The Advocate', and 'The Spirit of Christ' (concept 47) and Gal 4:6 sit in other concepts. Do not add a John 16:14-15 line to concept 22 or 47 without the matching 'from the Father' texts beside it; leave it as is.

Concept 50 (closing hope): Romans 15:13 sits after Galatians 5:5 in the list; if the site orders passages canonically within a concept, put Romans 5:5, 8:23 and 15:13 before Galatians 5:5. The concept meets the rule: hope words from passages within the theme, and the dark concepts (8, 9, 10, 11) are kept as their own sub-themes.

Capitalisation caveat across the outline (Reformed, Orthodox, academic): the Berean writes 'Spirit' where the Greek has pneuma without telling the reader whether it is the Holy Spirit. After the drops above, Rom 2:29 and 7:6 (concept 34), Rom 8:15 and Eph 1:17 (concepts 43, 3) still rest on it. They are fine under their own concepts because the name carries the capital from 2 Cor 3:6 or Rom 8:15, but note it for the check against MACULA.

Secondary 'Breath': add Genesis 2:7 ('breathed into his nostrils the breath of life') and Isaiah 42:5, which a reader of Spirit-as-breath would look for first; they are in the texts' words and need no gloss.

Secondary 'Anointing': 1 John 2:20 and 2:27 ('you have an anointing from the Holy One') are the other anointing passage a reader would look for; the Berean does not name the Spirit in them, so only add if the owner accepts it as a word-for-word anointing link.
Secondary 'Laying on of hands': add Acts 9:17 (Ananias lays hands on Saul that he be filled with the Holy Spirit), which is already in concept 26.
Links: no change. 'Baptism' (if a theme) would be the one a Baptist or Catholic reader looks for from concepts 19, 27 and 28; add only if such a theme exists.
Order of the concepts: no side is taken. The run from 24 (promise) through 26 (filled), 27 (fell upon) and 28 (gift) does not imply a sequence of experiences; leave the order as drafted.

missing.sub_theme: Gifts and the one who gave them
missing.why: Concept 30 lists only the 1 Cor 12 gifts. A reader of the Spirit theme expects the other gift lists the texts give (apostles, prophets, teachers, helps; 'to each one grace has been given'); these are the verses where cessationist, continuationist and Orthodox/Catholic readers all look. They do not all name the Spirit, so keep them as a separate plain-labelled concept with their own wording, e.g. 'There are different gifts' is already used; use 'gifts differing according to the grace given' or 'He gave gifts to men'. Note that Eph 4 and Rom 12 do not mention the Spirit in the verses, so show only the verses' words.

The seer's 'in the Spirit' states run through Revelation (1:10, 4:2, 17:3, 21:10) and a reader would expect them together with Ezekiel's 'the Spirit lifted me up'. Only 17:3 is in concept 7. Keep 17:3 there and let the others form this short concept, or add 4:2 and 21:10 to concept 7 and drop the idea of a separate one.

missing.sub_theme: through the eternal spirit / vindicated by the spirit / made alive in the spirit (lower-case plain label)
missing.why: These four are the New Testament's lines on Christ's own resurrection and offering 'in/through' a spirit, and a reader of this theme (Reformed, Catholic, Orthodox, Pentecostal) expects them; they are dropped from concepts 17 and 33 on the grounds above, but the texts plainly develop the sub-theme. Keep the name lower-case and plain (e.g. 'In the spirit' in the Berean's words, not 'the Spirit') because readers part on whether each names the Holy Spirit; do not interpret.
